question.leadin: During this war, UN forces were set back to a 140-mile defense line known as the "Pusan Perimeter" due to multiple defeats by the KPA.
question.text: Name this 1950s war that never ended with a peace treaty, but instead with the establishment of the DMZ. The U.S. and Soviet Union divided the namesake country of this war along the 38th parallel.
question.clue: A commander on one side of this war proposed dropping 30 to 50 nuclear bombs on an opponent in order to create a radioactive wasteland and was criticized for rudeness to his country's leader at Wake Island.

swap.leadin: Operation Paul Bunyan involved the use of overwhelming military force to chop down a tree in this area.
swap.text: Name this area which separates North and South Korea from each other. The Joint Security Area within this zone is used for diplomatic meetings.

question.leadin: Name these places identified with the Korean War.
question.text: This village in the DMZ was the location of the peace talks between the two sides, and talks still go on just outside this village.
question.clue: This village which hosted a more famous conference that led to the armistice between United Nations forces and communists in 1953 during the Korean War.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about a certain class of warship.
swap.text: An earlier example of an ironclad warship was this type of ship developed by Admiral Yi Sun-sin to resist a 16th century Japanese invasion of Korea. Named for the shape of the animal on its bow, these ships boasted cannons and a hull covered in spikes.
swap.clue: Soldiers from Ming China helped defend Korea from Japanese invasion at the end of the 16th century. During that conflict, Korean Admiral Yi utilized these crazy awesome vessels which received their name from the appearance caused by their armored decks.

question.text: During the lead up to this time period, the forces of Sun Quan and Liu Bei used fire ships to turn back the much larger force of Cao Cao at the Battle of Red Cliffs. This time period followed the collapse of the Han dynasty.
question.clue: The "Later" part of a period with this name was dominated by a Unified Silla that conquered Goguryeo.

swap.text: The Three Kingdoms period consisted of clashes between the Silla, Goguryeo (koh-KUR-yoh), and this Korean state in the southwest, which was governed from Hansong and was ruled by Geunchogo (gwen-CHOH-goh).
swap.clue: This kingdom absorbed all of the lands of the Mahan confederacy, thus seizing all of the present-day Jeolla ("jul-lah") region, under its great ruler Geunchogo ("geun-choh-goh").

question.leadin: The first president of this nation was overthrown in the April Revolution because he rigged the election.
question.text: Name this nation that disputes the possession of the Liancourt Rocks with an eastern neighbor.
question.answerHtml: South Korea (accept Republic of Korea, prompt on Korea)
question.clue: This country's first female leader led it from 2013 until her 2017 impeachment.

swap.leadin: U.S. naval forces have been involved in multiple incidents in Asia. answer the following.
swap.text: In 1968, the USS Pueblo was attacked by vessels from this country off of Ryo Island near Wonsan. That country still holds the Pueblo to this day in its Victorious War Museum.
swap.clue: This country's first leader proposed the "Juche" ideology.

question.text: This fourth emperor of the Joseon dynasty is credited with developing the phonetic Hangul writing system in the 1400s, though yangban elites resisted the change.
question.clue: Under the guidance of his father, this man launched an expedition against a polity controlled by So Sadashige that had become a base for pirates; that assault on Tsushima was the Oei invasion.

swap.leadin: Time to see how much you know about East Asian naval battles.
swap.text: In this last stand of the Korean navy, Admiral Yi Sun-Sin defeated a Japanese fleet of over 10 times his size with only 13 ships, destroying half the Japanese fleet. It is widely regarded as his greatest victory.
swap.clue: Joseon was invaded twice by Toyotomi Hideyoshi's forces in the Imjin War but were driven back at this 1597 naval engagement by Admiral Yi Sun-sin despite the Japanese outnumbering the Korean fleet at least 10 to 1.

question.leadin: Name these Asian politicians who had European wives.
question.text: This first president of South Korea assumed dictatorial powers when the Korean War broke out, and was exiled with his Austrian wife Franziska Donner to Hawaii after his overthrow in a 1960 coup.
question.clue: Jimmie Leach observed his crackdown of the April 3rd uprising on Jeju Island.

swap.text: This longest Korean dynasty was later established when its King Taejo ("TAY-jo") overthrew a Goryeo ("GORE-yo") king loyal to the Mongols. Sejong the Great developed the hangul alphabet during this dynasty.
swap.clue: As he died, a military leader of this kingdom instructed, "Beat my war drums. Do not announce my death."

question.text: The Korean peninsula was introduced to Buddhism from China in the fourth century CE by Sundo, who mainly proselytized in this kingdom. Baekje, Silla, and this kingdom comprised the Korean Samhan.
question.clue: Some of the best-preserved art of this kingdom survives in the tomb of Dong Shou at a complex at Anak.

swap.text: Members of this Joseon noble, scholarly class were expected to be knowledgeable in the Confucian classics. To enter this class, one had to perform well on the gwageo civil service exam.
swap.clue: Seowon [suh-wun] were private schools constructed for the education of this class, which was wealthier than the sangmin [sahng-meen]. A genealogy book called a jokbo [choke-boh] could be used to prove one's membership in this Korean class.

question.leadin: This dynasty drew its civil servants exclusively from the aristocratic Yangban class, rather than the outcast Baekjeong.
question.text: Name this dynasty that ruled Korea using a strict caste system after coming to power in 1392 until it was overthrown by a Japanese invasion in 1910.
question.clue: This dynasty was destabilized by succession crises called the Strifes of the Princes.

swap.text: The successful repulse of Japan extended the rule of this dynasty, under which the Hangul alphabet was created. It ruled until Japan finally conquered the peninsula in 1910.
swap.clue: Once led by Sejong the Great, this dynasty promulgated the hanggul script and pursued an isolationist policy that led it to be known as the "hermit kingdom."

question.leadin: Guerrillas in this uprising set up bases in the caves around Hallasan, an extinct volcano where remains of victims can still be found, and attacked paramilitary troops of the Northwest Youth League.
question.text: Name this massacre that lasted over a year from April 1948 to 1949, in a nation being occupied under Operation Blacklist Forty.

swap.leadin: Identify the following about Korean history FTPE.
swap.text: This first native Korean state arose near the Yalu River in the first century CE and conquered the Chinese colony of Lolang.
swap.clue: Under Yang, China attempted to conquer this kingdom, which opposed Baekje and Silla during the Korean Three Kingdoms Period. That invasion failed after the Battle of the Salsu River.

question.leadin: Now located at the National Library of France, it was composed by the Buddhist monk Baegun around 1372 AD, and published by his students Seoksan and Daldam. FTPE.
question.text: Name this two-volume Korean anthology of Zen Buddhist teachings which is the oldest existing metal-plate printed book.

swap.leadin: It began when Wang Kon united the kingdoms of Goguryeo, Silla and Baekje.
swap.text: Name this Korean dynasty that reigned from 918 to 1392.
swap.clue: Twenty-nine women from hojeok ("HO-juck") families were married to this dynasty's founder, Wang Geon ("gun").
